universal.notes: First ordinary Gef lesson. It teaches the level system used by books, learner profiles, placement, and future Gefstimates. Priority 0 is reserved for a future prerequisite-level orientation such as 'What is a language?' if Gef ever authors one; do not invent a placeholder lesson merely to fill zero.

Universal grammatical-gender comparison family. Runtime eligibility and Core/Full readiness come from the universal Lesson SSOT plus lesson-specific language capabilities; global language tier alone never grants support.

Family path stage 1: Core family. Pair-level session depth determines Core versus Cultural. If either source or target role is Tier 3/comparison-only, show only the localized Core lesson and recognition-safe vocabulary/game material.
Family path stage 2: Describe your family. Canonical readiness and gaps are owned by curriculum/lesson-system-manifest.json.
Family path stage 3: Extended family. Canonical readiness and gaps are owned by curriculum/lesson-system-manifest.json.

Family path stage 4: Relationships and family life. Current 104-language Core vocabulary breadth remains intentionally partial where the SSOT says coverage is not yet proven; do not fake missing translations.
Names, transliteration, related historical forms, and naming practices. Cultural claims remain community-sourced and candidate until reviewed.
A1 clock-time and day-period concept lesson. Core can use the shared temporal teaching surface universally; target-language phrasing and day-period boundaries remain reviewed language/context data.

A1 weekday-cycle lesson. Calendar first-day layout remains territory/locale context rather than a language fact. The shared temporal surface provides day/week navigation without changing the canonical teaching order.
A1 month-cycle implementation. It is paired with LES.mul.time.calendar_years inside the canonical Months and years lesson part.
A1 calendar-year reference implementation. Calendar system, era, numeral, and spoken year conventions remain explicit context/review data rather than bare-language assumptions.
A1 season vocabulary. Hemisphere, climate, and traditional seasonal systems remain contextual instead of being inferred from a language tag.

Universal semantic-map primer for meanings English often gives to 'for'. Structural gold-standard family; review state remains candidate and Tier 3 never inherits Full grammar support from Core comparison coverage.
Universal grammatical-number comparison lesson. Core comparison and Full target eligibility are resolved from lesson-specific capability data and the universal Lesson SSOT.
Optional cross-language semantic overview only. It no longer owns scored sequential practice; the CEFR-bounded Being lessons do.
A1 Being stage 1: identity, classification, and ordinary properties.
A2 Being stage 2: current/resultant states plus entity and event location distinctions where licensed.
A2 Being stage 3: existence, absence, and conditional possession-as-existence comparisons.
Later/optional Being stage for time/date, origin/affiliation, and material predication when the target language makes those comparisons pedagogically useful.

language_specific.notes: Spanish-specific Full implementation inserted by the canonical Spanish learning-path override immediately after the universal multiple-words-for semantic primer. Practice exists; reader/default-reading evidence remains review-gated.

path_policy.tier1: Build an ordered curriculum that may interleave lessons and story/chapter recommendations. Full grammar path is expected over time.
path_policy.tier2: Build a selective ordered curriculum that may interleave reviewed lessons and story/chapter recommendations when evidence supports them. Do not imply a complete grammar path.
path_policy.tier3: Reading and games remain the main learning path, but universal topical lessons may expose explicitly bounded Core sessions. Core availability must never be mistaken for full cultural or grammar-course support.
path_policy.next_resolution: After a lesson completes, prefer the next explicit item in the active language path. If no language-path successor exists, fall back to the next eligible compatibility-catalog item by ascending priority. If neither exists, return to the originating lesson/dashboard context.
